attacks.claim: The takedown test checks only that one wildcard invalidation was issued and that S3 keys are gone. It does not verify that CloudFront edge copies and the 60 s HTML cache stop serving the purged paths, so a legal takedown has no verified completion point.
attacks.evidence: Test: purge an image with a full responsive set; assert zero remaining keys and one wildcard invalidation.

attacks.claim: Re-encoding wire photos into new sizes and formats for the whole backfill rests on an internal photo-desk confirmation. No licence clause is cited and there is no legal sign-off, so the licence basis for roughly 310,000 images is unverified. Wire images should be excluded from derivative generation until this is attached.
attacks.evidence: Extra sizes and formats of the same licensed image for the same display use are covered by the current licences (photo desk confirmation on WEB-778, Oct 19).

attacks.claim: The plan does not say when has_responsive_set is set relative to successful upload of every derivative, nor how partial sets are cleaned up. If the flag is set after one format succeeds, the template emits picture sources that 404, and the retry path skips the image.
attacks.evidence: <picture> is rendered only when image.has_responsive_set is true (set by the task)... images with has_responsive_set already true are skipped; restarting is safe.

attacks.claim: 'Publishing tasks are never delayed' is asserted, not designed. The backfill runs on the same two worker nodes as publishing, and a separate Celery queue does not isolate CPU or memory. The plan names no concurrency cap, memory limit, or dedicated worker, so a heavy AVIF encode can starve publishing.
attacks.evidence: on a separate low-priority Celery queue, so publishing tasks are never delayed... Compute: existing worker nodes, off-peak; no new instances.

attacks.claim: The purge prefix '<id>-' is safe only if ids cannot contain '-' or be prefixes of other ids. The trailing hyphen gives partial protection, but the id format and length are not stated anywhere in the plan.
attacks.evidence: Keys share the image's existing prefix: media/2026/10/a81f3c-1600.jpg (existing)... delete every key under the image's <id>- prefix

attacks.claim: The success target (CrUX p75 mobile LCP ≤ 2.5 s) sits just below the prototype's WebPageTest p75 of 2.6 s, from 50 articles on one device profile. The measurement methods differ, and the plan gives no path to close the gap.
attacks.evidence: WebPageTest (Moto G Power, 4G, 3 runs per article): p75 LCP 3.9 s → 2.6 s... CrUX p75 mobile LCP on article pages ≤ 2.5 s within 6 weeks of 100%.

attacks.claim: Backfill needs about 9.7 h inside a 10 h two-night window with no failure budget or retry allowance. The 100% rollout step is not gated on backfill completion, so a stalled backfill leaves many articles on plain img while the success measure is read as if the change shipped.
attacks.evidence: 0.9 s per image for the full set (prototype, c6i.xlarge). Two existing worker nodes × 4 workers ≈ 9.7 h... 10% of articles → 50% → 100% over one week

attacks.claim: libvips 8.14 parses HEIC, AVIF and WebP on every upload. VIPS_BLOCK_UNTRUSTED restricts loaders but does not patch parser bugs. The plan does not say workers restart after unattended-upgrades, so a patched library may not be loaded.
attacks.evidence: libvips 8.14 from the Debian 12 package (LGPL-2.1, dynamically linked; security updates via unattended-upgrades)... workers run with VIPS_BLOCK_UNTRUSTED=1.

attacks.claim: Each re-crop mints a new id with a full set of about 11 derivatives, and superseded ids are never deleted. Storage grows with edit history. The plan's own growth figure is small (about $0.07/month), so this is a retention-policy gap, not a blocker.
attacks.evidence: Re-crops already create a new image id (new keys)... Derivatives can stay in S3 or be deleted by prefix later

attacks.claim: The ~340 KB per-image figure is not derived from the listed outputs. The two 800 px derivatives alone total about 149 KB (61 KB AVIF + 88 KB WebP), before the 480, 1200 and 1600 px variants and the 800 px JPEG. The storage total and the ~9,000 uploads/month input are likely understated and unsourced.
attacks.evidence: ~340 KB of new derivatives per image → ~105 GB... 800 px AVIF median 61 KB, WebP 88 KB... ~9,000 new uploads

attacks.claim: The 21 TB to 9 TB and ~$1,000/month CloudFront saving is extrapolated from the 50-article prototype and presented as a cost headline. The plan labels it an estimate, so it should not be used for budgeting before the 30-day measurement.
attacks.evidence: projected ~9 TB by applying the prototype's byte savings to September's traffic mix, ≈ $1,000/month less. This is an estimate

attacks.claim: The JPEG srcset omits the 1600 px candidate, so 2x devices at the 720 px column get at most 1200 px JPEG and reach 1600 px only through AVIF or WebP. The srcset and format candidate sets do not match.
attacks.evidence: with the JPEG srcset; src is the existing 1600 px JPEG... sizes="(max-width: 720px) 100vw, 720px"

attacks.claim: The metadata test covers a GPS/XMP/IPTC fixture only. It does not state coverage for HEIC inputs, which upload validation accepts, or for embedded thumbnails, which are where identifiers often survive.
attacks.evidence: New test: build every derivative from a fixture carrying GPS EXIF, XMP and IPTC; assert none of it survives in any output.

attacks.claim: Rollout buckets by article id, but has_responsive_set is per image, and images can be shared across articles. A page can mix responsive and plain states during backfill, which confounds the 10/50/100% RUM comparison.
attacks.evidence: bucketed by article id so a given page is consistent and cacheable... comparing RUM LCP and CLS between groups at each step

attacks.claim: width and height come from stored dimensions, which may be the original rather than the crop rectangle. If the crop changes aspect ratio, the reserved box disagrees with the derivative and CLS can regress against the ≤0.05 target.
attacks.evidence: keeps the existing alt... gains width/height from stored dimensions to prevent layout shift.

attacks.claim: The RESPONSIVE_IMAGES setting has no named owner, change log, or record of the live rollout step, so rollback decisions depend on unrecorded state.
